title: IV fluid tonicity

findings.where: Images 1, 5, 6, 8, 12 and 13: 'Bags by in-bag osmolarity'; tonicity.jsx LISTS, fact 5 and Frame description
findings.title: The osmolarity table uses tonicity category names
findings.problem: The table explicitly classifies osmolarity but labels its rows 'Isotonic', 'Hypotonic' and 'Hypertonic'. Fact 5 likewise calls D5W 'isotonic in the bag', while the bags caption more precisely says 'about iso-osmolar'. These are familiar nursing conventions, but switching terminology undermines this diagram's explicit distinction between osmolarity and effective tonicity.
findings.fix: Title the existing table 'Conventional nursing bag classifications' and retain the dextrose caveat. If the heading remains specifically about osmolarity, use osmolar terminology with appropriate approximate/product-dependent qualifiers. Use 'about iso-osmolar in the bag' consistently for D5W.

assessment: No blocker identified. One terminology inconsistency remains in the bag classification.
